[[File:Quinn Chapel of the A.M.E. Church (10564193663).jpg|thumb|left|Carmy's [[The Bear season 1|season 1]] Al-Anon meetings were filmed at [[Quinn Chapel AME Church (Chicago)|Quinn Chapel AME Church]] in [[Bronzeville (Chicago)|Bronzeville]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Golden |first=Jamie Nesbitt |date=April 18, 2024 |title=Chicago's Oldest Black Church Is Now Debt-Free |url=https://blockclubchicago.org/2024/04/18/chicagos-oldest-black-church-is-now-debt-free/ |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=Block Club Chicago |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 6, 2018 |title=Early Chicago: Quinn Chapel |url=https://www.wttw.com/dusable-to-obama/quinn-chapel |access-date=2026-01-07 |website=[[WTTW Chicago]] |language=en}}</ref>]]
Behaviors exhibited throughout the series and personal characteristics he mentions in a [[monologue]] at an [[Al-Anon/Alateen|Al-Anon]] meeting in season one (including difficulties paying attention, difficulties in school, and difficulties making friends) suggest to some viewers that Carmy should be categorized as a [[neurodivergent]] person.<ref name="CarmyAlAnon-108">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1fjITOkFnnE |title=Carmy's 7-Minute Monologue |date=July 13, 2022 |last=FX Networks |access-date=2025-09-02 |via=YouTube}}</ref><ref name="lr">{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Micah |date=September 19, 2022 |title=Let It Rip: Hulu's ''The Bear'' |url=https://fnewsmagazine.com/2022/09/let-it-rip-hulus-the-bear/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=F Newsmagazine |language=English |archive-date=2025-06-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250616125719/https://fnewsmagazine.com/2022/09/let-it-rip-hulus-the-bear/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In season 5, Richie describes him as "differently abled."<ref name="ribs504-transcript">{{Cite web |date=June 30, 2026 |title=The Bear - S05E04 - Ribs - Transcript |url=https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/the-bear-s05e04-ribs-transcript/ |access-date=2026-07-07 |website=Scraps from the loft |language=en-GB}}</ref> Some observers have asserted that Carmy exhibits symptoms of [[complex post-traumatic stress disorder]] (CPTSD).<ref name="Kumar-2025">{{Cite web |last=Kumar |first=Ravi |date=July 24, 2025 |title=Under Pressure: A Psychologist's Take on Carmy from ''The Bear'' |url=https://nymentalhealthcenter.com/under-pressure-a-psychologists-take-on-carmy-from-the-bear/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=NY Mental Health Center |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250808135545/https://nymentalhealthcenter.com/under-pressure-a-psychologists-take-on-carmy-from-the-bear/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="lr" /><ref name="Padua-2026">{{Cite web |last=Padua |first=Laura |date=2026-01-26 |title=Let It Rip: Trauma, Control, and Complex PTSD in The Bear |url=https://www.spiegeloog.amsterdam/let-it-rip-trauma-control-and-complex-ptsd-in-the-bear/ |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=Spiegeloog |language=en-US}}</ref> Plagued with [[Perfectionism (psychology)|perfectionism]] and unresolved [[grief]] over Mikey's suicide,<ref name="Longeretta-2023">{{Cite web |last=Longeretta |first=Emily |date=August 4, 2023 |title=Oliver Platt Talks 'Complexity' of Playing Uncle Jimmy on ''The Bear'': 'You Don't Know If He's Going to Shake You or Give You a Hug' |url=https://variety.com/2023/tv/awards/oliver-platt-uncle-jimmy-the-bear-1235683763/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250210172510/https://variety.com/2023/tv/awards/oliver-platt-uncle-jimmy-the-bear-1235683763/ |archive-date=2025-02-10 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=Variety |language=en-US}}</ref> Carmy compartmentalizes his feelings in favor of the grinding labor of the kitchen and periodically sabotages his own happiness in order to minimize his potential exposure to ''any'' emotion.<ref name="Jensen-2024">{{Cite web |last=Jensen |first=Erin |date=July 3, 2024 |title=There's a reason ''The Bear'' makes you anxious: We asked therapists to analyze Carmy |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/entertainment/tv/2024/07/03/the-bear-season-3-carmy-analyzed-real-therapists/74279135007/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=USA TODAY |language=en-US}}</ref> 

He had a pronounced [[Stuttering|stutter]] in childhood; [[Speech disfluency|verbal disfluency]] re-emerges in the adult Carmy when he is exposed to people or situations that remind him of the neglect and abuse of his youth.<ref name="Gilbert-2024">{{Cite web |last=Gilbert |first=Sophie |author-link=Sophie Gilbert |date=July 8, 2024 |title=Why ''The Bear'' Is So Hard to Watch |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2024/07/the-bear-fx-season-3-carmy-trauma/678938/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=The Atlantic |language=en |archive-date=2024-08-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240801142009/https://www.theatlantic.com/culture/archive/2024/07/the-bear-fx-season-3-carmy-trauma/678938/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Naming and articulating his feelings, and speaking up for himself in the face of [[Manipulation (psychology)|emotional manipulation]], remain enduring challenges for Carmy; he "stutters and staggers" through interpersonal relationships, falling back on "I'm trying" when he fails to reveal himself or connect with his nearest and dearest.<ref name="ig"/><ref name="Ruiz-2025">{{Cite web |last=Ruiz |first=Rebecca |date=July 3, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season 4 finally moves into the light |url=https://mashable.com/article/the-bear-season-four-trauma |access-date=2025-09-29 |website=Mashable |language=en}}</ref> As a rule, Carmy cannot or will not talk much, preferring to show rather than tell. As White put it in 2023, he is "not a vocal person, not a great communicator."<ref name="GoldDerby-2023"/> He has exacerbated his existing social struggles with a habit of viewing professional colleagues as competitors and threats to be defeated.<ref name="yg" />  

For its part, the show demonstrates that the mad genius is entirely dispensable if other members of the crew have been fully trained and amply empowered.{{Sfnp|Flores Jurado|2024|p=18}} Much of Carmy's counterproductive season 3 pursuit of a brittle sort of perfection seemingly stemmed from a mistaken belief that "if he can cook well enough, if he can be the best, then he can give the people he cares about what they need. And if he destroys himself in the process, then that only proves how much he loves them. Then, at least, he wouldn't feel like he failed them."<ref name="al" /> The show  deconstructs Carmy's [[messiah complex]], instead emphasizing "the absurdity, and damage, of the [[auteur theory]] of anything{{mdash}}greatness is never a solitary achievement."<ref name="McNamara-2025">{{Cite web |last=McNamara |first=Mary |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Commentary: By taming its chaos, ''The Bear'' bravely shows us what addiction recovery looks like |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/tv/story/2025-06-27/the-bear-season-4-addiction-recovery |access-date=2025-09-24 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> A consistent and deeply sincere [[Apology (act)|apologizer]], by season 4, his transgressions against those closest to him have become too consistent for his apologies to hold much weight; Richie yelled in recrimination that "your sorries mean shit."<ref name="pr" /> Carmy does keep his [[Promise|promises]] to his staff: for instance, in the pilot he told Marcus he would get him a new [[Mixer (appliance)|mixer]], and the Bear has a $14,000 Varimixer, and in the seasons 3 and 4 premiere episodes he promised the staff a Michelin star, and they got two.<ref name="toboc-508transcript" />

[[File:Mr. Beef Chicago Illinois.jpg|thumb|Mr. Beef in Chicago partially inspired the fictional Original Beef of Chicagoland restaurant depicted on ''The Bear'']]

== Relationships ==
According to a Chicagoan writing in ''[[The New York Times Magazine]]'', Carmy's decision to step out of the New York City fast lane to "dole out unglamorous sandwiches from a broken-nosed kind of shop" rewrites his career trajectory: "Carmy went back to Chicago because he had to. He stays because he wants to...the point is to do a great thing, for its own sake, alongside people you care about, without much concern for image or status. ''The Bear'' seems to see this as a very Chicago thing."<ref name="ac"/>

=== Natalie ===
Carmy and his surviving sibling, older sister Sugar, are quite close and have a warm, sensitive, funny relationship.<ref name="McCarthy-2024Elliott">{{Cite web |last=McCarthy |first=Amy |date=July 1, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Star Abby Elliott Studied Up for Her Role as Restaurant Manager |url=https://www.eater.com/24187597/the-bear-abby-elliott-studied-for-her-role-restaurant-manager-houstons |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=Eater |language=en-US |archive-date=2024-07-06 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240706003512/https://www.eater.com/24187597/the-bear-abby-elliott-studied-for-her-role-restaurant-manager-houstons |url-status=live}}</ref> "Shug," as he calls her, looks out for his emotional well-being and eventually gets involved in running the family restaurant, a business she had loathed when it was under Michael's management.<ref name="Grebenyuk-2025Elliott">{{Cite web |last=Grebenyuk |first=Yana |date=September 16, 2025 |title=Abby Elliott Addresses ''The Bear''{{'s}} Future — And Spinoff Ideas — After Season 5 |url=https://www.usmagazine.com/entertainment/news/abby-elliott-addresses-the-bears-future-and-spinoff-ideas-after-season-5/ |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=Us Weekly |language=en-US}}</ref> According to White, Carmy often "feels incapable of reaching back, or being like, accepting" of Sugar's love, whereas Elliott has suggested that Sugar's expressiveness sometimes comes from a place of desperation, "like, 'Please don't leave me here with our family.'"<ref name="Ortiz-2024">{{Cite web |last=Ortiz |first=Andi |date=June 27, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Stars Jeremy Allen White and Abby Elliott Break Down That Emotional Sibling Flashback |url=https://www.thewrap.com/the-bear-season-3-episode-1-jeremy-allen-white-abby-elliott-interview/ |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=TheWrap |language=en-US}}</ref>

=== Richie ===
Richie and Carmy call each other ''cousin'' even though they are not biologically related.<ref name="to">{{Cite web |last=Hadadi |first=Roxana |date=June 29, 2022 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} Ebon Moss-Bachrach on the Art of Playing the Obstacle |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-ebon-moss-bacharach-interview.html |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=2025-09-16  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250916134848/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-ebon-moss-bacharach-interview.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Richie was a long-time manager of the Beef alongside Mikey.<ref name="to"/> He ran the place with "F-bomb-dropping, gun-toting swagger."<ref name="fd">{{Cite web |last=McNamara |first=Mary |date=June 28, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' isn't about the pressures of fine dining. It's about the damage alcoholism inflicts |url=https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/tv/story/2024-06-28/alcoholism-addiction-the-bear-season-3 |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |language=en-US}}</ref> Richie initially resented that the restaurant had been bequeathed to the long-absent Carmy instead of to him. Richie led the vanguard of the kitchen's opposition to Carmy's succession to his brother's throne; he declares that Carmy's years of nearly militaristic discipline and grueling labor have made him "pretentious, delusional, and a fucking sissy."<ref name="mc">{{Cite web |last=Antista |first=Lucia |date=May 26, 2024 |title=The Bear and Others: A Study on Masculinity in Crisis |url=https://medium.com/@lucia_antista/the-bear-and-others-a-study-on-masculinity-in-crisis-0669864f2b02 |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Medium |language=en}}</ref> According to White, despite their feuding within the restaurant, "For Carmy, Richie is the closest thing to Michael and vice versa. I think Carmy would have a hard time letting him go and I don't think that Richie would go willingly, either."<ref name="Rice-2022">{{Cite web |last=Rice |first=Lynette |date=December 3, 2022 |title=''The Bear'' Star Jeremy Allen White on Working on The Line and Finding the Right Recipe for the Kitchen Industry |url=https://deadline.com/2022/12/the-bear-jeremy-allen-interview-1235183587/ |access-date=2025-12-05 |website=Deadline |language=en-US |archive-date=2023-03-14  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230314181042/https://deadline.com/2022/12/the-bear-jeremy-allen-interview-1235183587/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

Carmy and his de facto foster brother, Richie, are prone to "emotional suppression and self-destruction...shouting matches and belittl[ing] one another," habits of [[toxic masculinity]] and [[patriarchy]] learned at home and at work.<ref name="fl">{{Cite magazine |last=Schaab |first=Kate |date=August 12, 2025 |title=FX's ''The Bear'' Season 4 Embraces Feminist Leadership, Challenging Aggressive Masculinity and Reimagining the Workplace |url=https://msmagazine.com/2025/08/12/the-bear-season-4-review-women-sydney-natalie-carmen-berzatto/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |magazine=Ms. Magazine |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250822233316/https://msmagazine.com/2025/08/12/the-bear-season-4-review-women-sydney-natalie-carmen-berzatto/ |url-status=live}}</ref> These behaviors hobble them individually and the functioning of the business generally, but they simultaneously encourage and enable the careers of their female partners.<ref name="fl"/> One rundown of ''The Bear'' characters prior to season four described Richie as "Carmy's arch-fremisis," a [[portmanteau]] constructed from [[frenemy]] and [[arch-nemesis]].<ref name="Karlton-2025chars">{{Cite web |last=Jahmal |first=Karlton |date=June 19, 2025 |title=Before ''The Bear'' Season 4 Drops, Here's A Quick Character Recap |url=https://www.buzzfeed.com/karltonjahmal/the-bear-season-4-quick-character-recap |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=BuzzFeed |language=en |archive-date=2025-08-18  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250818192357/https://www.buzzfeed.com/karltonjahmal/the-bear-season-4-quick-character-recap |url-status=live }}</ref> The Carmy–Richie fight club never seems to end, but when asked in 2025 by ''Interview'' magazine who would win a fight between [[List of Shameless (American TV series) characters#Lip Gallagher|Lip Gallagher]] of ''[[Shameless (American TV series)|Shameless]]'' and Carmy of ''The Bear'', Allen picked Lip, saying "Carmy doesn't want to fight anybody. He's all bark, no bite."<ref name="Interview2025">{{cite web |last=Interview |url=https://www.tiktok.com/t/ZTMHoXyk4/ |title=''Interview'' Post 6: Jeremy Allen White |date=October 23, 2025 }}</ref>

=== Claire ===
During season 2, Carmy had a sexual relationship with emergency room physician [[Claire Bear (The Bear)|Claire]] ([[Molly Gordon]]) over the course of four or five episodes ("[[Pop (The Bear)|Pop]]" to "[[Omelette (The Bear)|Omelette]]"), or six weeks. The pair first met as teenagers and have overlapping social circles.<ref name="Betancourt-2025Clairmy">{{Cite web |last=Betancourt |first=Bianca |date=June 30, 2025 |title=Can ''The Bear'' Stop Trying to Make Carmy and Claire Happen? |url=https://www.harpersbazaar.com/culture/film-tv/a65210772/the-bear-carmy-claire-relationship-controversy-explained/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Harper's Bazaar Magazine |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-05  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250805095721/https://www.harpersbazaar.com/culture/film-tv/a65210772/the-bear-carmy-claire-relationship-controversy-explained/ |url-status=live }}</ref> One season 2 reviewer commented, "...that storyline just doesn't get the attention it deserves. And besides, we already know that Carmy's real love is this restaurant, even if it does torture him. On some level, Claire's sporadic appearances prove that even Carmy knows that to be true."<ref name="em"/> According to ''[[Grub Street (website)|Grub Street]]'', dating a chef can apparently be quite frustrating, in part because a "laser-focused, hypercompetitive kitchen addict is not necessarily able to become a different person when they come home, especially if they're exhausted."<ref name="Lopez-2022">{{Cite web |last=Lopez |first=Nastassia |date=August 1, 2022 |title=Everyone's Thirsty for ''The Bear''. Here's What It's Really Like to Date a Chef. |url=https://www.grubstreet.com/2022/08/what-it-would-really-be-like-to-date-a-chef-from-the-bear.html |access-date=2026-10-16 |website=[[Grub Street (website)|Grub Street]] |language=en}}</ref> Chefs can be unpleasant critics of both home cooking and restaurant food, their schedules often do not leave much time for family events like weddings and holidays, and when they do come home, they often arrive "smelling like onions and fryer oil."<ref name="Lopez-2022" />

Carmy "personally serve[d] Claire and her friend as a kind gesture" at the restaurant's soft launch, but "his head [was] echoing with negative thoughts and terrible self-criticisms."<ref name="Gonzalez-2023">{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez |first=Erica |date=June 23, 2023 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} Season 2 Finale Serves Dinner with a Side of Disaster |url=https://www.elle.com/culture/movies-tv/a44320947/the-bear-season-2-ending-explained-recap/ |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=ELLE |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-08-21  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250821202216/https://www.elle.com/culture/movies-tv/a44320947/the-bear-season-2-ending-explained-recap/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Upon returning to the kitchen he seemingly retreated to the walk-in fridge to collect himself, and got locked inside because of the broken door handle. Service was a success without him, and Tina told Carmy that everyone was OK, but he was consumed with shame and guilt for not being present in the kitchen: "I failed you guys."<ref name="gs">{{Cite web |last=Nemetz |first=Dave |date=June 25, 2023 |title=''The Bear''Finale Recap: Opening Night Shivers — Plus, Grade Season 2 |url=https://www.tvline.com/recaps/the-bear-recap-season-2-finale-episode-10-opening-night-1235004908/ |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=TVLine |language=en-US}}</ref> Talking his way through it alone in the fridge, Carmy concluded that his personal relationships were at fault: "No amount of good is worth how terrible this feels."<ref name="gs" /> In the meantime, Carmy's T had been replaced on the other side of the door by Claire, who was disappointed in what she heard.<ref name="gs" /> She walked away, kissing cousin Richie a forlorn goodbye on the way.<ref name="gs" /> ''The New York Times'' described Claire as "never-quite-a-girlfriend."<ref name="Murray-2025">{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Noel |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Did ''The Bear'' Bounce Back? Sort of, Chef |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/27/arts/television/the-bear-season-4-recap.html |access-date=2025-10-19 |work=The New York Times |language=en |archive-date=2025-09-20  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250920203032/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/27/arts/television/the-bear-season-4-recap.html |url-status=live }}</ref> [[Time (magazine)|''TIME'']] described Claire, compared to Chef Adamu, as a "more obvious" candidate for an onscreen romance with Carmen.<ref name="Mendez-2023time">{{Cite magazine |last=Mendez |first=Moises II |date=June 23, 2023 |title=Should We Ship TV Characters? Viewers of The Bear Have Feelings |url=https://time.com/6289867/the-bear-sydney-carmy-ship/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250516082606/https://time.com/6289867/the-bear-sydney-carmy-ship/ |archive-date=2025-05-16 |access-date=2025-09-21 |magazine=TIME |language=en}}</ref> While doing publicity for season 5, when asked about Claire and Carmy, White said, "I'm rooting for everybody. I'm a fan of everybody."<ref name="AccessHollywood-2026">{{Cite web |title=Jeremy Allen White had nothing... |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/DZsPamTk1vX/?stkn=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ== |access-date=2026-09-10 |publisher=[[Access Hollywood]] |via=[[Instagram]]|date=June 17, 2026}}</ref>

=== Sydney ===
The "brilliant" Sydney has been described as Carmy's "most valued colleague."<ref name="pr"/><ref name="fd"/> Syd is "an ambitious black girl who trained at the [[The Culinary Institute of America|Culinary Institute of America]]."{{Sfnp|Grazia Serra|2024|p=118}}{{efn|Syd's Blackness and her family tree has been little explored outside of her self-expression through hair and clothing styles, at least until the season four episode "[[Worms (The Bear)|Worms]]," but she is possibly [[Nigerian Americans|Nigerian-American]]. Carmy is [[White American|White]] under the current racial filing system.<ref name="Lincicome-2023">{{Cite web |last=Lincicome |first=Scott |date=July 12, 2023 |title=''The Bear'' Is a Tribute to Dynamism–and What Blocks It: The regulatory nightmare of opening a restaurant |url=https://www.cato.org/commentary/bear-tribute-dynamism-what-blocks-it |access-date=2025-10-26 |website=cato.org |archive-date=2025-11-18  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251118094715/https://www.cato.org/commentary/bear-tribute-dynamism-what-blocks-it |url-status=live }}</ref>}} Syd's presence has also been described as perhaps filling "the void his brother Michael left, but in a much healthier way."<ref name="cr">{{Cite web |last=Bhatt |first=Jinal |date=June 27, 2024 |title=I'm Willing to Wait for a Syd and Carmy Romance on ''The Bear'' |url=https://www.themarysue.com/syd-carmy-romance-the-bear-season-3-willing-to-wait/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250126091543/https://www.themarysue.com/syd-carmy-romance-the-bear-season-3-willing-to-wait/ |archive-date=2025-01-26 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=The Mary Sue |language=en}}</ref> Carmy and Sydney have a deeply familiar, vulnerable, and often emotionally fraught partnership.<ref name="Mattson-2024">{{Cite web |last=Mattson |first=Kelcie |date=July 2, 2024 |title=Sydney Needs to Escape from The Bear |url=https://collider.com/the-bear-season-3-sydney/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250711021631/https://collider.com/the-bear-season-3-sydney/ |archive-date=2025-07-11 |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref> Among other things, Syd "asserts a brand of female partnering we rarely get to see in popular culture. When Carmy flubs, Sydney challenges him. When she has better ideas, she speaks up. She recognizes his immaturity, selfishness and even his demons, and rarely lets him off the hook. She knows what he's capable of and holds him to a commensurate standard."<ref name="Warrell-2023">{{Cite news |last=Warrell |first=Laura |date=July 7, 2023 |title=Why did seeing a strong Black woman on ''The Bear'' make me cry? |department=Opinion |url=https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2023-07-07/the-bear-hulu-carmy-sydney-claire-black-women-tv-ayo-edebiri |access-date=2025-09-17 |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-02-22 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222215913/https://www.latimes.com/opinion/story/2023-07-07/the-bear-hulu-carmy-sydney-claire-black-women-tv-ayo-edebiri |url-status=live}}</ref>

That there are romantic nuances to their relationship has been denied by show runners and actors. In 2023, executive producer [[Joanna Calo]] recounted that at one pointed she had pitched Syd and Carmy eventually kissing, and "'Chris was like, 'No!' [...] And he was totally right, but I think what I was getting at was that these relationships are complicated. I've heard people use the term '[[work wife]]'{{mdash}}there are relationships in our lives that have all different meanings, and we sometimes really rush to characterize everything very cleanly. There's something beautiful about acknowledging how messy our lives really are and just how enmeshed so many of our relationships are."<ref name="Guy-2024">{{Cite web |last=Guy |first=Zoe |date=June 27, 2024 |title=Every Time They Told You It Isn't Going to Happen |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-carmy-sydney-romance-fans.html |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=2025-06-27 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250627021828/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-carmy-sydney-romance-fans.html |url-status=live}}</ref> In 2025 Edebiri told a reporter, "I do think it's professional, and I do think if anything were to happen, it would not be the show that we're making. And I also think it would be so crazy. That man is crazy and that girl is a bad communicator! The restaurant would blow up in like three seconds if anything ever happened."<ref name="Garner-2025">{{Cite web |last=Garner |first=Glenn |date=August 24, 2025 |title=Ayo Edebiri Shoots Down ''The Bear'' Romance for Syd & Carmy: 'The Restaurant Would Blow Up' |url=https://deadline.com/2025/08/ayo-edebiri-shoots-down-the-bear-romance-syd-carmy-1236496247/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=Deadline |language=en-US}}</ref> She elsewhere described Marcus's devotion to [[Jelly doughnut|jelly-filled doughnuts]] as the show's "sexiest relationship."<ref name="Guy-2024" /> When asked about Luca (Will Poulter) as an alternative romantic prospect for Sydney, Edebiri said "I don't know. Maybe they're just two [[Libra (astrology)|Libras]] having a conversation? Who's to say, I don't have the scripts."<ref name="Ford-2025">{{Cite web |last=Ford |first=Rebecca |date=August 19, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Made Ayo Edebiri a Star—and Now a Director |url=https://www.vanityfair.com/hollywood/story/hollywood/story/ayo-the-bear-directing |access-date=2026-09-10 |website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2026, White told an interviewer that while restaurants are a "really great environment for drama and comedy and all this stuff. [...] the show, to me, could almost take place anywhere [...and is] about finding purpose, and passion, knowing what you're capable of, and how you can kind of show up for that, [... it's] a show about inspiration..."<ref name="TheWrapJAW-2026">{{Cite web |publisher=[[TheWrap]] |date=June 16, 2026 |title=Jeremy Allen White shares... |url=https://www.threads.com/share/BBr_hPws4k/ |access-date=2026-09-10 |via=[[Threads (social network)|Threads]]}}</ref>

One critic, arguing that fan opposition to a "Carmy and Sydney" pairing may have its roots in [[misogynoir]], or unconscious biases about what relationship roles are "appropriate" for Black women, commented that "Sydney and Carmy's very {{Linktext|slow burn}} is underlined by Carmy and Claire's very fast burn."<ref name="Omowale-2024">{{Cite web |last=Omowale |first=Jendayi |date=June 24, 2024 |title=Do ''The Bear'' Fans Know Protesting SydCarmy Is Kinda Racist? |url=https://www.teenvogue.com/story/the-bear-fans-opposing-sydcarmy-exposing-racism-op-ed |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=[[Teen Vogue]] |language=en-US}}</ref> A counterargument acknowledged the romantic prospects of the pairing and asserted that "SydCarmy is a product of [[social media]], an arena where floating bigoted takes prompts engagement. A wound-up [[Shipping (fandom)|shipping]] contingent guarantees a vocal opposition will materialize," whereas that the authentic argument against romantic consummation is not racialized or gendered but an out-of-hand rejection of the "indolent model in [[Romantic comedy|romantic comedies]] that posits love can fix anything," all while "some viewers also search for signs of developments we want to see, producing the ever-widening rift between those who want Carmy and Syd to stay [[Plato's number|platonic]] and the SydCarmy masses yearning for the two to [[kiss]] already."<ref name="bp">{{Cite web |last=McFarland |first=Melanie |date=June 29, 2024 |title="The Bear" brings Syd and Carmy to a boiling point, but we're throwing cold water on the ship |url=https://www.salon.com/2024/06/29/the-bear-brings-syd-and-carmy-to-a-boiling-point-but-heres-why-they-cant-be-endgame/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=ogshare&utm_content=og |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=[[Salon.com]] |language=en-US}}</ref> NPR critic-at-large Eric Deggans noted after the series finale that TV series "which turn on whether the lead characters will connect romantically—called 'will they or won't they' stories—tend to fall apart after romance is consummated," a peril avoided by ''The Bear''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Deggans |first=Switching Codes w/Eric |date=2026-06-29 |title=Why ''The Bear'' series finale works so well: A story about found family that really stuck the landing |url=https://ericdeggans.substack.com/p/why-the-bear-series-finale-works |access-date=2026-10-04 |website=Switching Codes w/Eric Deggans}}</ref>

|language=en}}</ref><ref name="sh">{{Cite web |last=Cadenas |first=Kerensa |date=December 4, 2023 |title=When Did Shows and Movies About Food Get So Horny? |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=[[The Daily Beast]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="cs">{{Cite web |last1=Marlow |first1=Erin |last2=Temis |first2=Carla |date=November 27, 2025 |title=Special Episode: |url-status=live }} – [https://podcasts.apple.com/us/podcast/special-episode-the-syd-carmy-special/id1493022117?i=1000738803354 Episode on Apple Podcasts]</ref> describing "stolen glances...mutual hyperaware of her."<ref name="cs" /> He also seemingly has a knack for soothing her insecurities; when she confesses a fear in season 2 that she will "just fuck up and fail" he promises her, "I won't The show is also laden with barely-[[Sublimation (psychology)|sublimated]] sensuality (the pair frequently hover over "sizzling meat and simmering sauces"),<ref name="Wickes-2022">{{Cite web |last=Wickes |first=Jade |date=July 20, 2022 |title=''The Bear'': how a show with no sex got the internet so horny |url=https://theface.com/culture/the-bear-how-a-show-with-no-sex-got-the-internet-so-horny-jeremy-allen-white-carmy-ayo-edebiri-sydney-second-season-tv-relationships |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250712035313/https://theface.com/culture/the-bear-how-a-show-with-no-sex-got-the-internet-so-horny-jeremy-allen-white-carmy-ayo-edebiri-sydney-second-season-tv-relationships |archive-date=2025-07-12 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=The Face |language=en-gb}}</ref> and visual [[innuendo]]es.<ref name="cr" /> The pair's kitchen jargon naturally lends itself to horny [[Double entendre|double-entendres]] ("Hands!" "Behind!" "Yes, chef.").<ref name="Stevens-2022slang">{{Cite web |last=Stevens |first=Ashlie D. |date=July 20, 2022 |title=Why is everyone so horny for kitchen slang? the summer."<ref name="Greenblatt-2022">{{Cite web |last=Greenblatt|first=Leah|date=August 3, 2022|title=Checking in with ''The Bear''{{'s}} Ebon Moss-Bachrach|url=https://ew.com/tv/the-bear-ebon-moss-bachrach-richie-interview/|website=Entertainment Weekly}}</ref> The kitchen parlance of ''The Bear'' rapidly "made its way into dirty talk,"<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kickham |first=Dylan |date=2022-07-11 |title=Chef-Speak Is Taking Over Twitter Thanks To 'The Bear' |url=https://www.elitedaily.com/entertainment/the-bear-chef-speak-tweets-memes/amp |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=Elite Daily |language=en}}</ref> and appeared as the post-coital [[Punch line|punchline]] of a [[New Yorker cartoon|''New Yorker'' cartoon]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Flake |first=Emily |author-link=Emily Flake |date=2022-07-25 |title=Daily Cartoon: "So... what was all that 'Yes, Chef' stuff about?" |url=https://www.newyorker.com/cartoons/daily-cartoon/monday-july-25th-yes-chef |magazine=The New Yorker |language=en-US |issn=0028-792X}}</ref> Scenes between the two alone together are often punctuated by lines that could be read unplatonically—Carmy prompts her to go out with him by saying "You should come," and he surfaces some of his old rage to insist, "I'm your fucking friend!"—and staging of scenes between the two chefs often "begs for an [[Eroticism|erotic]] reading."<ref name="bp" /> The under-the-table scene{{Em dash}}wherein Syd and Carmy are without any sex. Sensual music plays in the background...Then they switch positions (!) so that Carmy is on top and Syd is on the bottom."<ref name="Heifetz-2024">{{Cite web |last=Heifetz |first=Danny |date=June 25, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Is a Love Story. For his part, [[Anthony Bourdain]], one of the restaurant's patron saints, venerated with autographed pictures on the walls of the old Beef, argued that the relationship between a chef and his sous is often one of great intimacy: "My sous-chef, in an ideal situation, is like my wife. I'll go further: my sous-chef, in an ideal situation, is closer to me than my wife...All the things I couldn't do—or couldn't be seen to do—he did. And he did them well...Having a sous-chef with excellent cooking skills and a criminal mind is one of God's great gifts."<ref name="Bourdain-souschef">{{Cite book |last=Bourdain |first=Anthony |author-link=Anthony Bourdain |title=Kitchen Confidential |title-link=Kitchen Confidential |year=2008 |publisher=Bloomsbury Publishing USA |isbn=978-1-59691-724-8 |orig-year=2000}}</ref> The dynamic between the two has been described in multiple sources as "the beating heart of the show,"<ref name="Male-2025" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gelda |first=Revati |date=2026-02-18 |title=15 Moments that Prove Sydney and Carmy Should Be Together in The Bear |url=https://telltaletv.com/2026/02/15-moments-that-prove-sydney-and-carmy-should-be-together-in-the-bear/ |access-date=2026-10-11 |website=telltaletv.com |language=en-US}}</ref> with one writer arguing, "Their relationship feels specific and lived in, and as different as they are, Carmy and Syd compliment each other."<ref name="Male-2025">{{Cite web |last=Male |first=Victoria |date=August 24, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season 5 Update Avoids the Show's Biggest Carmy Mistake |url=https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/the-bear-season-5-update-avoids-the-shows-biggest-carmy-mistake/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=ComicBook.com |language=en-US |archive-date=2026-03-05  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260305135216/https://comicbook.com/tv-shows/news/the-bear-season-5-update-avoids-the-shows-biggest-carmy-mistake/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Other family, friends, and colleagues ===
The first name of the [["Pop" Berzatto|father of the Berzatto kids]] is unknown; he abandoned the family "probably sometime in the 1990s."<ref name="ft">{{Cite web |last=Friedlander |first=Whitney |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Yo...Cousin? A Guide to The Bear's Sprawling 'Family' Tree |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-characters-family-tree-season-4-guest-stars-explained.html |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=Vulture |language=en}}</ref> Upon returning to Chicago Carmy reconnected with Richie and Jimmy, but other, more distant, relatives and friends of the family charged him with being a "fuckin loser" for working in a restaurant, and conflated him with Mikey.<ref name="Eakin-2024dogs">{{Cite web |last=Eakin |first=Marah |date=June 3, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Recap Rewind: Who Puts Ketchup on a Hot Dog? |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-recap-season-1-episode-4-dogs.html |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=2024-12-26  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241226113619/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-recap-season-1-episode-4-dogs.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Carmy remained "[[Family estrangement|no contact]]" with his mother until near the end of season 4, when he visited her house for the first time in many years.<ref name="wc" /> 

In childhood, the three Berzatto siblings were known by nicknames suffixed with –bear: by [[birth order]], they were Mikeybear, Sugarbear, and Babybear.<ref name="fe">{{Cite web |last=Murray |first=Russell |date=January 31, 2025 |title=The Bear Family Tree: Every Member Of The Berzatto Family Explained |url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1773384/the-bear-berzatto-family-tree-explained/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=SlashFilm |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-02-01 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250201222353/https://www.slashfilm.com/1773384/the-bear-berzatto-family-tree-explained/ |url-status=live}}</ref> In adulthood Carm is still called Bear by his sister, others who knew him in his youth, and the restaurant's [[pastry chef]] [[Marcus Brooks]] ([[Lionel Boyce]]), in whom Carmy discovers another kindred spirit and culinary equal.<ref name="Tang-2023">{{Cite web |last=Tang |first=Terence |date=September 23, 2023 |title=10 TV Characters That Prove Introverts Are Great Too |url=https://screenrant.com/best-introvert-tv-characters/ |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=2023-09-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230930155426/https://screenrant.com/best-introvert-tv-characters/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="fe"/><ref name="Lamour-2024Boyce">{{Cite web |last=Lamour |first=Joseph |date=January 31, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' star Lionel Boyce is excited to film Season 3: It's like 'summer camp' |url=https://www.today.com/food/people/the-bear-lionel-boyce-season-3-rcna136598 |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=TODAY.com |language=en |archive-date=2025-07-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250703235256/https://www.today.com/food/people/the-bear-lionel-boyce-season-3-rcna136598 |url-status=live}}</ref> Chef Terry and [[Ebra]] both tend to call him by the more-formal Carmen, rather than Carmy. One of the cooks at the Beef, [[Tina Marrero]] ([[Liza Colón-Zayas]]), begins calling Carmy "Jeff" as a corruption of the more respectful title ''chef''; Jeff and extensions such as Jeffrey eventually come to be used as endearments, when Tina transfers her affection for the late Mikey to his younger brother Carmy.<ref name="TinaCarmyJeff-2023">{{Cite web |last1=Lealos |first1=Shawn S. |last2=Miller |first2=Abigail |date=September 13, 2023 |title=Why Tina Calls Carmy "Jeffrey" In The Bear |url=https://screenrant.com/why-tina-calls-carmy-jeffrey-the-bear-show/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=2024-07-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240704011334/https://screenrant.com/why-tina-calls-carmy-jeffrey-the-bear-show/ |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="ChiTrib-2025">{{Cite news |date=June 25, 2025 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} Colón-Zayas relishes playing a chef rooted in reality |first=Zareen |last=Syed |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/chicago-tribune-the-bears-coln-zayas-r/181270447/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] |pages=5–001}} & {{Cite news |title=Colón-Zayas (con't) |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/chicago-tribune-coln-zayas/181270269/ |work=Chicago Tribune |pages=5–004}}</ref> Close to Marcus, Tina, and Syd in particular, Carmy tortures himself with regret over supposedly having "failed them."<ref name="Galluci-2024">{{Cite web |last=Galluci |first=Nicole |date=June 27, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Season 3 Review: Carmy Secures His Role as the Chairman of the Tortured Chefs Department |website=Decider.com |url=https://decider.com/2024/06/27/the-bear-season-3-review-hulu-fx/ |access-date=2025-09-19 |language=en-US}}</ref>

In addition to Sugar, Marcus, Syd, Tina, and Richie on every third Thursday, Carmy has been supported by his compassionate and profane cousin Michelle Berzatto ([[Sarah Paulson]]),<ref name="oc">{{Cite news |last=Spencer-Elliott |first=Lydia |date=July 2, 2024 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} biggest cameos ranked, from Olivia Colman to Jamie Lee Curtis |url=https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/tv/features/the-bear-cameos-olivia-colman-jamie-lee-curtis-b2569371.html |access-date=2025-09-18 |newspaper=[[The Independent]] |language=en-gb |archive-date=2025-09-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250908204259/https://www.the-independent.com/arts-entertainment/tv/features/the-bear-cameos-olivia-colman-jamie-lee-curtis-b2569371.html |url-status=live}}</ref> who is good to Carmy and who encouraged him to escape the chaos of the family home in Chicago and continue to pursue his career as a chef.<ref name="Alexander-2025">{{Cite news |last=Alexander |first=Bryan |date=July 7, 2025 |title=Family gathers for a wedding on ''The Bear'' |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-columbus-dispatch-family-gathers-for/181280625/ |access-date=2025-10-19 |work=The Columbus Dispatch |type=Part 1 of 2 |page=D1 |location=Columbus, Ohio |agency=''USA Today'' Syndicate}} & {{Cite news |date=July 7, 2025 |title=The Bear (con't) |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-columbus-dispatch-the-bear/181279957/ |type=Part 2 of 2 |page=D2}}</ref> Michelle and her husband Stevie ([[John Mulaney]]) let Carmy crash on their couch while he worked in New York.<ref name="ft"/>

Andrea Terry, a sophisticated businesswoman who treats Carmy warmly and generously, and a culinarily skilled and socially sharp colleague known as [[Luca (The Bear)|Chef Luca]] ([[Will Poulter]]), both from Ever, remain influential in Carmy's life as well.<ref name="ft"/><ref name="oc"/> Luca, who fits in immediately and effortlessly with the staff of the Bear, "is cut from the same cloth as Carmy and is motivated by perfection and legacy more than money and taking the easy route to success."<ref name="MacArthur-2025poulter">{{Cite web |last=MacArthur |first=Greg |date=June 29, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season 4 Completely Justifies Will Poulter's Return For 3 Seasons In A Row |url=https://screenrant.com/the-bear-season-4-will-poulter-luca-stage-return-justified/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=2025-06-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250630031502/https://screenrant.com/the-bear-season-4-will-poulter-luca-stage-return-justified/ |url-status=live}}</ref> Similarly, while their social relationship is strictly restrained until after her retirement, Terry seems to have served as sort of surrogate mother figure who reparented Carmy by modeling the belief that "cooking for people...is 'time well spent'," whereas Donna saw cooking meals for her family as "only as time not recognized."<ref name="al"/>

=== Mikey ===
Mikey Berzatto's big personality and his final bequests to the baby of the family underlie Carmy's story, and resurface particularly in "Tomorrow" and "Goodbye," but "in both ''The Bear'' and ''[[Ted Lasso]]'', the suicide of a (male) loved one functions as [[backstory]] for the protagonist, rather than being interrogated explicitly...suicide is rendered motivator or plot device rather than situated as a tangible element of the text."<ref name="Wilkins-2025">{{Cite book |last=Wilkins |first=Christina |chapter-url=https://link.springer.com/10.1007/978-3-032-05442-5_5 |title=Male Mental Illness in Contemporary Culture: Anglo-American Representations, 2010 to Present |publisher=Macmillan Palgrave |year=2025 |isbn=978-3-032-05441-8 |page=152 |language=en |chapter=Television Approaches: The Problems of Genre and Culture |doi=10.1007/978-3-032-05442-5_5}}</ref> 

''The New York Times'' commended the visual storytelling of Carmy sending an [[SMS|SMS message]] while riding to work on the train in "Groundhogs," during "which we can see that he has been texting Mikey (and getting 'not delivered' notices) since his brother died."<ref name="Murray-2025bounce">{{Cite news |last=Murray |first=Noel |date=June 27, 2025 |title=Did ''The Bear'' Bounce Back? == Other attributes ==
Allen's portrayal of Carmy Berzatto has been described as "a realistic casting of ''that asshole''" common to high-intensity kitchens, although "''The Bear'' suggests that Carmy's going to be a different kind of leader, one who's learned from his own experience and wants to change the narrative instead of perpetuating it."<ref name="Brendlinger-2025">{{Cite magazine |last=Brendlinger |first=Jane |date=June 24, 2025 |title=A Real Line Cook Explains What ''The Bear'' Nails—and Overhypes—About Kitchen Life |url=https://www.foodandwine.com/the-bear-restaurant-work-6402770 |access-date=2025-09-02 |magazine=[[Food & Wine]] |language=en}}</ref> [[Daniel Patterson (chef)|Daniel Patterson]], a chef who worked with series creator Storer on a documentary before quitting to make sandwiches, surmised that Carmy's iconic look was intended to be, ultimately, deconstructed: "...for the real-life cooks watching the show who see Carmy{{mdash}}with his perpetual grimace, rock-star hair, and cigarette dangling from his pouty lips{{mdash}}and feel like they've had it with the [[Marco Pierre White]] bullshit, I get it. We've all seen it before."<ref name="Patterson-2022">{{Cite magazine |last=Patterson |first=Daniel |author-link=Daniel Patterson (chef) |date=July 28, 2022 |title=When I Watch 'The Bear,' I See My Life |url=https://www.esquire.com/food-drink/restaurants/a40707554/the-bear-carmy-chef-daniel-patterson/ |access-date=2025-10-04 |magazine=Esquire |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-10-18  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251018110731/https://www.esquire.com/food-drink/restaurants/a40707554/the-bear-carmy-chef-daniel-patterson/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Sexuality, aesthetics, sex appeal ===
In the pilot episode, "System," Tina declares that Carmy cuts vegetables like a bitch and Richie declares that training elsewhere made Carmy "pompous, and delusional, and a fucking gayrod," which are intended as bullying attacks on Carmy's "masculinity (and thus his capability as a leader and a provider)."{{sfnp|Di Maio|2025|p=112}} The issue is not so much his (undisclosed) [[sexual orientation]], per se, as his "manner and methods of running the kitchen...at odds with the practice and priority of the other kitchen staff."{{sfnp|Wang|2025|p=10}}

Patterson extended his description of Carmy as chef with the comment, "The sexy dirty chain-smoking rebel cook is both a cipher for bad-boy fantasies and apologia for white-boy bad behavior."<ref name="Patterson-2022" /> In regard to the "bad-boy fantasies," the character of Carmy provoked an [[ode]] in [[Bon Appétit|''Bon Appétit'' magazine]] to what is apparently a food-service industry [[stock character]], "Sexually Competent Dirtbag [[Line cook|Line Cook]]," about which it was written:<ref name="York-2022">{{Cite web |last=York |first=Sarah |date=July 18, 2022 |title=Everyone's Horny for the 'Sexually Competent Dirtbag Line Cook' |url=https://www.bonappetit.com/story/the-bear-hulu-sexy-dirtbag-cook |access-date=2025-09-21 |website=[[Bon Appétit]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

{{blockquote|text="If you've ever waited in vain for a text back from a man with no [[bed frame]] in his apartment, you're already pretty familiar with this type. Imagine no-bed-frame man, but he only drinks from plastic [[quart]] containers and cooks a [[Carbonara|spaghetti carbonara]] that will make you write in your journal for the first time since high school. Has he showered today? No. Are you going to be the one to change him and make him want to settle down? Also no!"<ref name="York-2022"/>}}

Carmy has been identified as the textbook model of a restaurant-kitchen resident [[lothario]]: "'This man does not have curtains in his apartment but he has a $1400 [[Boning knife|knife that is only for cutting fish]].'"<ref name="po">{{Cite web |last1=Kinsman |first1=Kat |last2=Ram |first2=Chandra |title=We Hit Pause Over and Over So You Can Own Carmy's Library—Here's Every Real Cookbook Spotted on 'The Bear' |url=https://www.foodandwine.com/all-the-cookbooks-on-carmys-bookshelves-in-the-bear-7557548 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250612131948/https://www.foodandwine.com/all-the-cookbooks-on-carmys-bookshelves-in-the-bear-7557548 |archive-date=2025-06-12 |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=Food & Wine |language=en}}</ref> (Carmy's apartment is thrift-store furnished, and he has access to a mid-1990s [[Plymouth Voyager|Plymouth Voyager Sport]].) Another analysis tagged him as a self-evidently attractive yet problematic {{Linktext|fuck boy}}, discernible as such by his "tattoos, disheveled hair, and 20-a-day habit."<ref name="sh"/><ref name="fb">{{Cite web |last=Tenreyro |first=Tatiana |date=June 28, 2022 |title=Jeremy Allen White in ''The Bear'' Looks Like the Type of Fuckboy Every Woman Knows |url=https://melmagazine.com/en-us/story/jeremy-allen-white-the-bear-thirst |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=MEL Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> One "particular screengrab" from the trailer engendered much online commentary about the sex appeal of sweaty season 1 Carmy; the key screengrab and associated [[Tweet (social media)|tweet]] was later resurfaced for further comment on a [[late-night talk show]].<ref name="fb"/><ref name="JAW-TonightShow2025">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pP3ERM6TRdE |title=Jeremy Allen White Reacts to The Bear Memes, Says Springsteen Movie Trailer Blew Up His Phone |date=June 26, 2025 |last=The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon |access-date=2025-10-26 |via=YouTube |archive-date=2025-10-24  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251024054600/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pP3ERM6TRdE |url-status=live }}</ref> In season 4, while talking to Richie at Tiff's wedding, there is a hint that Jimmy is aware of this type of fellow, and that he connects him to Carmy in the context of his relationship with Claire: "I'm telling you, you and that fսckin' [[wikt:tweaked#English|tweaked-out]] line cook pal of yours, you're a pair of fսckin' idiots."<ref name=":1">https://tvshowtranscripts.ourboard.org/viewtopic.php?f=1396&t=74823 "Bears" 4x07</ref> The sweaty-line-cook visual seemed to surface, for some:<ref name="fb"/>

{{blockquote|text="...memories of fun-yet-questionable hookups...the kind of guy who'd fuck me by a dumpster after closing out the restaurant at 2&nbsp;a.m., sans [[condom]]. The irony is, the actual character, Carmy, doesn't fuck. He's so traumatized...that he has no energy for love. He can barely call his sister to check in on how she’s doing. It's likely that the last thing he's thinking about is getting laid. But it's understandable why, by looking at him, you'd think he's Chicago's hottest scumbag."<ref name="fb"/>}}

''MEL'' magazine commented "Carmy might not be the guy these women are projecting onto him, but admittedly, there's something hot about a man who is trying to get his shit together, too."<ref name="fb" /> In 2022, White denied the dirtbag charges against his character; he thought Carmy was meant to be understood as a "genuine and nice guy."<ref name="Selvam-2022JAW">{{Cite web |last=Selvam |first=Ashok |date=August 1, 2022 |title=''The Bear'' Star Jeremy Allen White on Why Carmy Is No Dirtbag |url=https://chicago.eater.com/2022/8/1/23287582/the-bear-star-jeremy-allen-white-hulu-reasons-that-carmy-is-no-dirtbag |access-date=2025-10-24 |website=Eater Chicago |language=en-US}}</ref> Per [[Salon.com]], Carmy's dirtbag subcategory would be "[[hero]]ic," in company with [[Cassian Andor]] of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe, as Carmy solved "a riddle left by his brother. === Home ===
Carmy has an apartment somewhere in Chicago, possibly in the [[Near West Side, Chicago|West Loop]] or [[Wicker Park, Chicago|Wicker Park]].<ref name="Konrad-2025">{{Cite web |last=Konrad |first=Erin |date=July 27, 2025 |title=Could ''The Bear''{{'s}} Carmy Afford His Chicago Loft Apartment on a Chef's Salary? |url=https://collider.com/the-bear-carmy-chef-salary-explained/ |access-date=2026-01-17 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Monteil-apt">{{Cite news |last=Monteil |first=Abby |title=This TikToker Discovered That He Lives in Carmy's Apartment from ''The Bear'' |date=June 28, 2023 |url=https://www.apartmenttherapy.com/the-bear-carmy-apartment-tiktok-37271582 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250115104016/https://www.apartmenttherapy.com/the-bear-carmy-apartment-tiktok-37271582 |archive-date=2025-01-15 |access-date=2026-01-17 |work=Apartment Therapy |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Yassine-2025">{{Cite web |last=Yassine |first=Leen |date=March 18, 2025 |title=Where's ''The Bear'' Filming? Unlike the restaurant where his most significant professional and personal relationships unfold, his flat is a space that is rarely explored."{{Sfnp|Nikolova|2025|p=46}}

=== Hair and costuming ===
A photo of London chef Marco Pierre White on the cover of ''The Devil in the Kitchen'' inspired Carmy's hairstyle in season 1.<ref name="Garcia-2022sugar">{{Cite web |last=Garcia |first=Kelsey |date=July 26, 2022 |title=Jeremy Allen White Knows Carmy Needs a Hairnet |url=https://www.popsugar.com/beauty/the-bear-jeremy-allen-white-hair-48898636 |access-date=2025-12-05 |website=Popsugar |language=en |archive-date=2024-06-25  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240625025340/https://www.popsugar.com/beauty/the-bear-jeremy-allen-white-hair-48898636 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Bellot-2023">{{Cite web |last=Bellot |first=Carmen |date=June 27, 2023 |title=An Ode to Chef Style |url=https://www.esquire.com/uk/style/a44195816/best-dressed-chefs/ |access-date=2025-12-05 |website=Esquire |language=en-GB |archive-date=2025-10-10  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251010171317/https://www.esquire.com/uk/style/a44195816/best-dressed-chefs/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Rice-2022"/> Carmy's default plain white [[T-shirt]] suggests to some that the show styles him as a "[[James Dean]] of the kitchen pass."<ref name="ts"/> (''The Bear'' uses a handful of T-shirt brands for Carm but most prominently one produced by German textile company [[Merz b. Schwanen]]).<ref name="ts">{{Cite news |last=Wolfson |first=James |date=October 15, 2022 |title=The most talked about T-shirt on TV |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-guardian-the-most-talked-about-t-shi/180234865/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |work=[[The Guardian]] |pages=19}}</ref> The look is understated to the point of being simple, but still evocative: "Looking closer at the details, this is a very well-fitting tee, hitting at a nice point on the bicep as well as a nice flattering point at the waistline where they should. The other thing is care. It is hardly ever stained. It takes a skilled chef to be able to always wear white tees, not stained."<ref name="fm"/>

=== Scars and tattoos ===
Carmy has at least two visible scars that have drawn comment from other characters: one on the inside of his left bicep, and one on the palm of his right hand. Chef Fields mocks his "cool scars" in episode 2, "[[Hands (The Bear)|Hands]]."  

{{Anchor|Carmy's tattoos}}
Carmy has nine tattoos that have been seen on the show. Tattoos are common among the "creative and rebellious" chefs who staff American restaurants.<ref name="Habib-2021">{{Cite web |last=Habib |first=Ayesha |date=September 14, 2021 |title=Chefs Answer the Common Question: Why Do So Many of Them Have Tattoos? |url=https://nuvomagazine.com/magazine/volume-24/chefs-answer-the-common-question-why-do-so-many-of-them-have-tattoos |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=NUVO |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-12-13  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251213162332/https://nuvomagazine.com/magazine/volume-24/chefs-answer-the-common-question-why-do-so-many-of-them-have-tattoos |url-status=live }}</ref> White said in 2022 that the tattoos were "for Carmy...sort of an armor, and I don't think he felt that tough all the time, and that got him here."<ref name="lw">{{Cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zs9QzIf3ZQ8 |title=10 Things Jeremy Allen White Can't Live Without |date=August 25, 2022 |last=GQ Magazine |access-date=2025-10-18 |via=YouTube}}</ref> In the time looping episode "Tomorrow," Carmy's visible tattoos track his career progression; for instance, in the scenes set at French Laundry at the beginning of his career, he has no tattoos yet on his fingers or on the backs of his hands.

# ''SOU'' tattoo, on the fingers of his left hand just above his knuckles; SOU could be the beginning of ''soul'', is pronounced like the beginning of ''soup'' or ''sous-chef'', but stands for "sense of urgency," which is a catchphrase used in Thomas Keller restaurant kitchens.<ref name="Plante-2022">{{Cite web |last=Plante |first=Chandler |date=August 8, 2022 |title=The Tattoo Artist For ''The Bear'' Reveals His Favorite Carmy Tattoos |url=https://www.popsugar.com/beauty/the-bear-tattoo-artist-interview-48911465 |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=Popsugar |language=en |archive-date=2025-07-02  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250702202621/https://www.popsugar.com/beauty/the-bear-tattoo-artist-interview-48911465 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="ct">{{Cite web |last=John |first=Sarah |date=July 1, 2025 |title=The Stories Behind All of Carmy's Tattoos on ''The Bear'' |url=https://www.thedailybeast.com/obsessed/the-bear-the-stories-behind-all-of-carmys-tattoos/ |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=The Daily Beast |language=en |archive-date=2025-11-10  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251110044329/https://www.thedailybeast.com/obsessed/the-bear-the-stories-behind-all-of-carmys-tattoos/ |url-status=live }}</ref> (''The Bear'' creator [[Christopher Storer]] directed a [[Documentary film|documentary]] on Keller called ''Sense of Urgency''.)<ref name="SRcarmytats">{{Cite web |last1=Sharma |first1=Dhruv |last2=Russell |first2=Tom |last3=Bruce |first3=Amanda |date=June 29, 2023 |title=''The Bear'': Carmy's 8 Tattoos & Their Meaning Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/the-bear-carmy-tattoos-meaning-explained/ |access-date=2025-10-18 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=2026-02-16  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260216081925/https://screenrant.com/the-bear-carmy-tattoos-meaning-explained/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

=== Religious and ethnic background ===
The Berzattos are [[Italian Americans|Italian American]] by heritage; media critics have found that the show traffics in stereotypes of Italian Americans being primarily consumed with gangsterism, "food and sex," but that Carmy's "pervasive/invasive relationship with family emerges as the theme of the series."{{Sfnp|Grazia Serra|2024|p=118}} As former Chicago resident [[Chris Witaske]] (who plays Carmy's brother-in-law Pete) put it in 2023, "I also think ''The Bear'' really captures how in Chicago you're all on top of each other all the time. It creates these really strong bonds of friendship and family. I always talk about how, in [[Los Angeles|L.A.]], if you want to see your friends you have to make plans and then stick to the plans and then drive 30 minutes. In Chicago, you walk down the street and see half your friend group and then go into a bar and everybody else is there. It's a tighter-knit community."<ref name="Eakin-2023witaske">{{Cite web |last=Eakin |first=Marah |date=July 5, 2023 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} Chris Witaske on Being the Berzattos' Pain Sponge |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-chris-witaski-pete-season-two-finale-fishes-interview.html |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=2023-07-18 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230718035321/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-chris-witaski-pete-season-two-finale-fishes-interview.html |url-status=live}}</ref> 

Unlike his older brother Mikey, Carmy himself has "no [[Stereotype|stereotypically]] Italian American features{{Em dash}}[he is] [[blond]], [[Eye color|blue-eyed]], with a constant astonished expression on his face, his attractiveness deriving from boyish appearance, barely counterbalanced by numerous tattoos and tight muscles."{{Sfnp|Grazia Serra|2024|p=121}} The Berzattos have a [[Catholic Church|Roman Catholic]] religious background.<ref name="hb">{{Cite web |last=McCabe |first=Brigid |date=July 21, 2023 |title=In Hulu's ''The Bear'', a little Catholic imagery goes a long way |url=https://www.americamagazine.org/arts-culture/2023/07/21/bear-catholic-imagery-245712/ |access-date=2025-09-02 |website=America Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> The family celebrates the [[Feast of the Seven Fishes]]; Carmy and his siblings sometimes make a ritual appeal to Our Mother of Victory, an embodiment of the [[Mary, mother of Jesus|Virgin Mary]].<ref name="hb"/><ref name="saunders-2008">{{Cite web |last=Saunders |first=William P. |date=October 8, 2008 |title=Our Lady of Victory, pray for us |url=https://www.catholicherald.com/article/columns/our-lady-of-victory-pray-for-us/ |website=Catholic Herald}}</ref>

=== Artwork and food journals ===
A less-publicized aspect of his creativity is his skill as a visual artist; Carmy fills a series of food journals "with beautiful drawings of ingredients he's worked with and meals he's imagined."<ref name="al">{{Cite web |last=Schwertner |first=Danielle |date=September 9, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Might Not Be A Love Story, But It Is A Story About Love |url=https://templeofgeek.com/the-bear-might-not-be-a-love-story-but-it-is-a-story-about-love/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=TEMPLE OF GEEK |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-05-05 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250505194509/https://templeofgeek.com/the-bear-might-not-be-a-love-story-but-it-is-a-story-about-love/ |url-status=live}}</ref> 

His artwork first appears in passing in the pilot, where his [[Architectural drawing|elevation sketch]] of the Bear is visible in the bathroom of the Beef, but this picture is not identified as Carmy's work until season 2's "[[Fishes (The Bear)|Fishes]]." Later in the second season Carmy shows drawings of proposed dishes to Sydney; he could not cook in their restaurant that had no gas line, so he sketched them, which "established just how good of an artist he is...Season 3 really emphasized this, with flashbacks to his time working at esteemed restaurants showing how he'd create intricate drawings of various dish ideas."<ref name="Bythrow-2025">{{Cite web |last=Bythrow |first=Nick |date=July 8, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season 5 Must Address Carmy's Forgotten Passion |url=https://screenrant.com/the-bear-season-5-carmy-art-passion-explore/ |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=ScreenRant |language=en |archive-date=2025-07-22  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250722010627/https://screenrant.com/the-bear-season-5-carmy-art-passion-explore/ |url-status=live }}</ref> 

[[File:Square crop straighten autotune Orf3us Lille Langebro bridge Copenhagen.jpg|thumb|While in Copenhagen, Carmy journals on [[Lille Langebro]] ({{translation|little long bridge}}), which is for foot and bicycle traffic. [[Langebro]], the next bridge over, is for automobiles.]]
Carmy's food journaling is depicted most extensively in the "[[Tomorrow (The Bear)|Tomorrow]]" and "[[Apologies (The Bear)|Apologies]]" flashback scenes, and then Donna pages through the books when visiting the Bear in season 5, with shots that depict previously unseen dishes, including what might be the grapefruit scallop that Sydney called the best bite she ever had.<ref name="ribs504-transcript" /> In Copenhagen he appears to use Leuchtturm1917 journals from a company based in [[Geesthacht]], near [[Hamburg]], Germany.<ref name="Makalintal-2024"/> His Ever journal is a [[Moleskine]]. One of his mentors, Chef Terry, noticed his artwork, and it may have influenced her decision to refer him for further training in Copenhagen.<ref name="Bibby-2024">{{Cite web |last=Bibby |first=Daniel |date=June 27, 2024 |title=The Bear Season 3, Episode 1 Timeline Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/the-bear-season-3-episode-1-timeline-explained/ |access-date=2025-10-28 |website=[[Screen Rant]] |language=en}}</ref> In seasons 3 and 4, Marcus frequently refers to Carmy's old notebooks, four of which he stores in the office at the Bear: ''Carmy/Copenhagen'', ''Carmy New York'', ''Carmy'' ''Daniel Boulud'', and ''Carmy – The French Laundry''. ''The Bear''{{'s}} Lisa Korpan-led art department teamed up to create Carmy's drawings and food journals through the end of season three.<ref name="ColorTimer-2024">{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Vincent |date=August 23, 2024 |title=Interviewing The Production Designer & Art Director For 'The Bear'|url=https://colortimerpodcast.mixinglight.com/episodes/interviewing-the-production-designer-art-director-for-the-bear |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=The Color Timer Podcast |language=en}}</ref> Chicago artist Denise Dietz was commissioned to create the "Sistine Chapel" artworks that Carmy showed Sydney "of the scripted dishes," when they did not yet have a functioning restaurant kitchen,"<ref name="ddinsta">{{Cite web |last=denisedietzart |date=June 29, 2023 |title=You guys! I was hired earlier this year to create some Sistine Chapel food drawings for The Bear! |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/CuFLuHUL4rU/?img_index=4&igsh=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ== |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=instagram.com}}</ref><ref name="ddinsta2">{{Cite web |last=denisedietzart |title=I did some drawings for The Bear |url=https://www.instagram.com/reel/C9GR-e7Pv6P/?igsh=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ== |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> and Abacuc Rodriguez "our in-house art department illustration star...kind of filled in all the other pages."<ref name="ColorTimer-2024"/><ref name="cocoinsta2024">{{Cite web |last=cuco4cocopuffs |date=July 2, 2024 |title=june 2024 _ s3 ❤️❤️❤️ |url=https://www.instagram.com/p/C87QHDGOCfV/?img_index=3&igsh=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ== |access-date=2025-11-10 |website=www.instagram.com}}</ref> In season 5, he leaves four of his journals behind at the Bear for Marcus, but not the most recent volume for his work at the Bear.<ref name="toboc508-transcript">{{Cite web |last= |date=July 3, 2026 |title=The Bear - S05E08 - The Original Beef of Chicagoland - Transcript |url=https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/the-bear-s05e08-original-beef-of-chicagoland-transcript/ |access-date=2026-07-06 |website=Scraps from the loft |language=en-GB}}</ref>

===Habits and props===
* '''Smoking:''' Carmy was a compulsive [[cigarette]] smoker for most of his adult life and into the first two seasons of the show. His cousin Stevie described Carmy as smelling, generally, like "[[Rush week|pledge week]] at a [[Sicilians|Sicilian]] fraternity...sweat, death, lemons, garlic...oh, and the ''most'' cigarettes."<ref name="Nemetz-2025wedding">{{Cite web |last=Nemetz |first=Dave |date=June 27, 2025 |title=The Bear Throws a Wild Wedding — and an Oscar-Winning Star Is Invited |url=https://www.tvline.com/recaps/the-bear-recap-season-4-wedding-episode-7-cast-brie-larson-1235467714/ |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=TVLine |language=en-US}}</ref> Carmy quit smoking in season 3, "Tomorrow," seemingly newly disgusted by the sight of a stub-filled ashtray left in the restaurant overnight.<ref name="fd"/> Carm started working [[Nicotine gum|nicotine-replacement gum]] as intensely as he once [[Tobacco smoking|burned tobacco]].<ref name="nicotinegum">{{Cite web |title="The Bear" season 3's best guest star? NRT gum |url=https://truthinitiative.org/research-resources/tobacco-pop-culture/bear-season-3s-best-guest-star-nrt-gum |access-date=2025-09-19 |website=truthinitiative.org |language=en}}</ref> He told Chi-Chi ([[Christopher Zucchero]]) that he was doing it to save the five minutes it takes to smoke,<ref name="next302-transcript">{{Cite web |date=June 27, 2024 |title=The Bear - S03E02 - Next - Transcript |url=https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/the-bear-s03e02-next-transcript/ |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=Scraps from the loft |language=en-GB |archive-date=2024-10-08 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241008065032/https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/the-bear-s03e02-next-transcript/ |url-status=live}}</ref> and he told Sydney he still thought about it, but "only every 10 seconds."<ref name="violet304-transcript">{{Cite web |title=S03E04 – Violet (Transcript) |date=June 27, 2024 |url=https://scrapsfromtheloft.com/tv-series/the-bear-s03e04-violet-transcript/}}</ref> The gum regimen and Carmy's determination to clean up his act seemingly worked to break the long-held habit, but he picked it up again in the season-four finale, "[[Goodbye (The Bear)|Goodbye]]," when novice Sydney, feeling "abandoned and enraged," inexplicably took up smoking, apparently driven by a combination of spite and nostalgia.<ref name="te">{{Cite web |last=Eakin |first=Marah |date=June 26, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season-Finale Recap: The Elephant in the Bear |url=https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-finale-recap-season-4-episode-10-goodbye.html |access-date=2025-09-20 |website=Vulture |language=en |archive-date=2025-06-28 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250628113836/https://www.vulture.com/article/the-bear-finale-recap-season-4-episode-10-goodbye.html |url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="eu">{{Cite web |last=Hailu |first=Selome |date=June 27, 2025 |title=''The Bear'' Season 4 Finale Recap: Where Do Carmy and Sydney End Up? * {{anchor|Sharpie}}'''Sharpies:''' [[Sharpie (marker)|Sharpie markers]] have a constant presence in Carmy's kitchen and character arc. In "Review" he barks orders about them ("Somebody get me a fucking Sharpie that fucking works!") and later whips one at Sydney's retreating form as she leaves him. In the words of one writer, "A Sharpie is never just a Sharpie...a Sharpie is an organizer. A Sharpie is a reminder that, as he tells his staff of chefs, consistency is the only way to level up...Sydney Adamu (Ayo Edebiri) forgets to turn off the pre-order option, Carmy lunges for a Sharpie to order the madness. However, it's not where it's supposed to be."<ref name="Paulson-2022">{{Cite web |last=Paulson |first=Dina |date=July 16, 2022 |title=''The Bear''{{'s}} Most Chaotic Episode Is All About the Character Tension |url=https://collider.com/the-bear-most-chaotic-episode-character-tension-explained/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Collider |language=en}}</ref> In a later episode, "Doors," Syd and Carm prep for a night of service,  Carmy makes the Sharpies are at hand and that Sydney has her customary Coke.<ref name="decider-doors">{{Cite news |date=June 28, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' Season 3 Episode 3 recap: "Doors" |url=https://decider.com/2024/06/28/the-bear-season-3-episode-3-recap/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250312171143/https://decider.com/2024/06/28/the-bear-season-3-episode-3-recap/ |archive-date=2025-03-12 |access-date=2026-09-18 |work=Decider |language=en-US}}</ref> In the same scene he notices she changed the document template for their order tickets; she tells him she made the margins wider because he writes notes in the margins (often with Sharpies, visible in flashback in episode 2 "Hands").<ref name="Rawls-doors2024">{{Cite web |last=Rawls |first=Murjani |date=June 29, 2024 |title=''The Bear'' S3E3 Review: Repetition Ain't All It's Cracked Up To Be |url=https://substreammagazine.com/2024/06/the-bear-review-season-3-episode-3-doors/ |access-date=2026-09-18 |website=Substream Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref>
* {{anchor|Tape}}'''Tape:''' "Sheridan" is the first episode where Carmy demonstrates cutting tape (rather than tearing it). When ''[[Food & Wine]]'' writers were indexing Carmy's bookshelves for an article "our editor-in-chief...said on [[Slack (software)|Slack]] when he saw the semi-incoherent shelving: 'Curious as to why Carmy obsesses over the perfect tape edges ''à la'' [[Sean Brock]] but not more rhyme or reason for his bookshelves.'"<ref name="po" /> An [[Eater (website)|''Eater'']] writer speculated that Carmy uses [[3M]] [[painter's tape]]; his preference for green is less common than the use of blue and is probably inherited from his old boss [[Chef David Fields]] ([[Joel McHale]]).<ref name="Makalintal-2024">{{Cite web |last=Makalintal |first=Bettina |date=June 28, 2024 |title=How to Shop ''The Bear'' Aesthetic |url=https://www.eater.com/24187593/where-to-buy-the-bear-clothes-dishes-cooking-tools-as-seen-on-hulu |access-date=2025-10-19 |website=[[Eater (website)|Eater]] |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-09-01  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250901143604/https://www.eater.com/24187593/where-to-buy-the-bear-clothes-dishes-cooking-tools-as-seen-on-hulu |url-status=live }}</ref> ''The New York Times''Wirecutter section surmised it was green FrogTape multisurface painter's tape.<ref name="wirecutter-2024" /> [[Thomas Keller]], of [[the French Laundry]] and [[Bouchon (restaurant)|Bouchon]] and [[Per Se (restaurant)|Per Se]], is known to prefer neon green tape.<ref name="food52tape-2016">{{Cite web |last=Stephens |first=Leslie |date=February 2, 2016 |title=The Kitchen Habit Professional Chefs Can't Stand |url=https://food52.com/story/15716-the-kitchen-habit-chefs-can-t-stand |access-date=2025-10-20 |website=[[Food52]] |language=en |archive-date=2025-09-01  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250901225501/https://food52.com/story/15716-the-kitchen-habit-chefs-can-t-stand |url-status=live }}</ref> According to ''[[Food52]]'', some professional kitchens have strict tape rules, such as: "...the tape has to get cut with a pair of scissors in a straight line, with a small tab folded over for ease of removal. On it should be written the product name, date, and initials of the person who packed the container."<ref name="food52tape-2016" /> Precise taping is thought to promote mental clarity in the kitchen and attention to detail in the dishes prepared and served at the restaurant.<ref name="food52tape-2016" /> One former line cook wrote in 2023, "I remember when I first learned the importance of cutting tape versus tearing it to make labels for my prep—this scene felt like such a key moment, as it's this attention to detail that propels the good chefs to award-winning chefs."<ref name="Bodden-2023">{{Cite news |last=Bodden |first=Lauryn |date=June 22, 2023 |title=6 Ways ''The Bear'' Gets Restaurant Culture Right, According to a Former Line Cook |url=https://www.thespruceeats.com/tv-show-the-bear-gets-restaurant-culture-right-5498898 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250418035152/https://www.thespruceeats.com/tv-show-the-bear-gets-restaurant-culture-right-5498898 |archive-date=2025-04-18  |access-date=2026-06-14 |work=The Spruce Eats |language=en |url-status=live }}</ref>
* '''Knives:''' Carmy's knives have been called part of a "profound gear-related story arc."<ref name="StJohn-2026">{{Cite web |last=St. John |first=Allen |date=June 26, 2026 |title=Yes, Chef! A Breakdown of the Best Kitchen Gear on ''The Bear'' |url=https://www.consumerreports.org/appliances/best-kitchen-gear-on-the-bear-a3285505470/ |access-date=2026-07-05 |website=[[Consumer Reports]] |language=en-US}}</ref> In the pilot, he searches for his lost knife, believing he is being hazed by the Beef cooks, but then spots it inadvertently knocked under a cabinet in the kitchen.<ref name="StJohn-2026" /> Carmy uses a hand-forged Japanese-made knife (''[[gyūtō]]'').<ref name="StJohn-2026" /> According to one source Carmy's knife is made by bladesmith Yoshimi Kato in Japan's [[Takefu Knife Village]].<ref name="StJohn-2026" /> According to another it is a Yoshimi Echizen knife that is usually only available in the United States through a single shop in [[Beverly Hills, California]].<ref name="Tingley-20232">{{Cite web |last=Tingley |first=Anna |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Every Single Knife Featured in ''The Bear'', And Where to Buy Them |url=https://variety.com/2023/shopping/news/the-bear-season-2-knives-where-to-buy-1235658066/ |access-date=2025-10-17 |website=[[Variety (magazine)|Variety]] |language=en-US |archive-date=2025-09-20  |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250920001925/https://variety.com/2023/shopping/news/the-bear-season-2-knives-where-to-buy-1235658066/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Whatever the source, he eventually gives it to Tina ("Yours, chef"), which has been called a "three-Kleenex moment."<ref name="StJohn-2026" />
